# Original media decoder fixtures

Author: OpenRPG Forge test contributors, 15 October 2026.
Licence: CC0-1.0, dedicated to the public domain for unrestricted test reuse.
No external game, purchased pack or Cadle content is used.

`tone.wav` is an original 256-frame, mono, 8 kHz, signed PCM16 signal. Sample
`n` is `round(1000 * sin(2 * pi * 440 * n / 8000))`. Python's standard-library
`wave` and `struct` modules wrote the RIFF file. This is a decoder test signal,
not artistic audio or proof of runtime playback.

`tone.ogg` and `tone.flac` were encoded locally with FFmpeg
`8.1.1-full_build-www.gyan.dev`, gcc 15.2.0. Only authored signal data is stored;
no executable or FFmpeg implementation is copied. Encoding commands:

```text
ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -nostdin -n -i tone.wav -map_metadata -1 -c:a libvorbis -q:a 3 -fflags +bitexact -flags:a +bitexact tone.ogg
ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -nostdin -n -i tone.wav -map_metadata -1 -c:a flac -compression_level 5 -fflags +bitexact -flags:a +bitexact tone.flac
```

Tests read the committed encoded bytes without requiring FFmpeg. PNG/JPEG
fixtures are generated by `image` from explicit original constant pixels.
GLB fixtures are authored in test code: an embedded triangle and a distinct
empty structural container. The latter explicitly has `has_geometry=false`
and is never evidence of a rendered model.

`floor0_invalid_book.ogg` is an original 241-byte adversarial Vorbis stream made
by the adjacent standard-library script `generate_floor0_fixture.py`. Its small
codebook is valid, while an audio packet selects book 31 from 16 Floor0 books.
The regression reproduced an unchecked decoder index. The admitted import
profile now accepts Floor1 only and refuses Floor0 before probing; this fixture
is not a supported playable audio asset. No decoder implementation is copied.
